evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: Bridget of York( 10 November 1480 – 1517) was an English princess, the tenth child and seventh daughter of Edward IV of England and Queen Elizabeth Woodville.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: She was the youngest sister of Elizabeth of York, Mary of York, Cecily of York, Edward V, Margaret of York, Richard of Shrewsbury, 1st Duke of York, Anne of York, George Plantagenet, 1st Duke of Bedford, and Catherine of York.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: She was also an aunt of Henry VIII of England.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: She was born in Eltham, London on 10 November 1480, and was baptised by Edward Story, Bishop of Chichester on 11 November 1480.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: Her godmothers at the baptismal fount were her paternal grandmother, Cecily Neville, Duchess of York, and her oldest sister, Elizabeth of York.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: Her godfather was William Waynflete, Bishop of Winchester.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: Bridget's aunt Margaret, Lady Maltravers, served as her godmother at her confirmation.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: Bridget was likely named after St. Bridget of Sweden.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: Her parents may have decided at the time of her birth that this daughter would be dedicated to a religious life, and Princess Bridget was entrusted to Dartford Priory, Dartford, Kent sometime between 1486 and 1492.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: She became a nun.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: Bridget maintained correspondence throughout her life with her sister Elizabeth of York, who also paid for her various minor expenses, as well as minor expenses of the orphaned Agnes of Eltham.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: After Bridget's sister, Elizabeth of York, married Henry VII, Elizabeth paid some of Bridget's expenses and kept in touch with her via messengers.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: Bridget is known to have left Dartford on at least one occasion, when she attended the funeral of her mother, Elizabeth Woodville, in 1492.

evidence.title: Bridget of York
evidence.text: She died about 1517.

evidence.text: Topham was married to Susan Micklethwait, daughter of Elias Micklethwait, York merchant and member of Parliament as well as twice the mayor of York.

evidence.title: Christopher Topham
